content.user_title: Guide CEO Strategy and Board Decisions
content.value_statement: Executives need structured support for strategy, governance, and stakeholder decisions. This skill provides frameworks, analyzers, and templates for clear CEO-level planning.
actual_capabilities: Summarizes CEO responsibilities, leadership routines, stakeholder priorities, and decision checkpoints.
Uses strategy_analyzer.py to score strategic health, risks, options, recommendations, and roadmaps.
Uses financial_scenario_analyzer.py to compare scenarios, NPV, IRR, runway, and risk-adjusted views.
Provides board calendar, board package, investor update, fundraising, and governance templates.
Includes culture, talent, reorganization, crisis leadership, and communication frameworks.
limitations: It does not provide legal, accounting, tax, or investment advice.
The analyzers use simplified models and depend on user-provided assumptions.
It does not fetch live market data or verify financial statements automatically.
Executive recommendations require review by leaders, finance, legal, and affected stakeholders.

use_cases.title: Plan quarterly CEO priorities
use_cases.description: Build a focused quarter plan with strategic goals, risks, metrics, and leadership routines.

use_cases.title: Prepare board and investor materials
use_cases.description: Create board packages, investor updates, decision requests, and follow-up actions from company context.

use_cases.title: Evaluate strategic options
use_cases.description: Compare expansion, acquisition, restructuring, or funding choices with risk, timing, and resource tradeoffs.

prompt_templates.title: Create a CEO priorities plan
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner planning for a quarter or month.
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me define CEO priorities for the next quarter. Company context: [stage, revenue, team size, market]. Include goals, risks, metrics, and weekly routines.

prompt_templates.title: Prepare a board update
prompt_templates.scenario: Board meeting preparation with known metrics.
prompt_templates.prompt: Draft a board update for [quarter] using these facts: [metrics, decisions, risks, asks]. Include a CEO letter, agenda, dashboard, and discussion topics.

prompt_templates.title: Analyze strategic options
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate comparison of several executive choices.
prompt_templates.prompt: Assess these strategic options: [options]. Compare investment, timing, risk, stakeholder impact, and decision criteria. Recommend a next step.

prompt_templates.title: Model an executive decision
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced decision support for a major company move.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the strategy and financial scenario frameworks to evaluate [major decision]. Include assumptions, scenarios, risk-adjusted tradeoffs, board questions, and an implementation plan.

output_examples.input: Prepare a board meeting package for a quarterly strategy review.
output_examples.output: A CEO memo outline, agenda, dashboard sections, risk register topics, decision requests, and follow-up actions.

output_examples.input: Compare aggressive, moderate, and conservative growth scenarios.
output_examples.output: A scenario summary with revenue, margin, runway, expected value, key risks, and recommended next actions.
A culture assessment plan, stakeholder communication map, transition risks, and a 90-day stabilization checklist.

best_practices: Provide current metrics, constraints, stakeholders, deadlines, and the decision owner.
Separate confirmed facts from assumptions before asking for recommendations.
Review outputs with finance, legal, people, and board stakeholders before action.
anti_patterns: Do not use vague company goals without metrics or decision criteria.
Do not treat outputs as legal, accounting, tax, or investment advice.
Do not share confidential board or investor data without required access controls.

faq.question: What does this skill help with?
faq.answer: It helps with CEO strategy, executive decisions, board governance, investor communication, financial scenarios, and organizational leadership.

faq.question: Can it run financial analysis?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes a local scenario analyzer for simplified projections, NPV, IRR, runway, and risk-adjusted comparisons.

faq.question: Does it replace an executive advisor?
faq.answer: No. It structures analysis and drafts materials, but leaders and qualified advisors must review decisions.

faq.question: What data should I provide?
faq.answer: Provide company stage, goals, metrics, financial assumptions, stakeholder needs, constraints, and the decision timeline.

faq.question: Can it prepare board materials?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes board agenda, package, dashboard, decision request, and investor update frameworks.

faq.question: Does it access live market data?
faq.answer: No. It uses included frameworks and user-provided inputs. Add current market data when needed.
